dishes.title: Red Wine Beef Stew (Target: 7R + 4L)
lines: **I. Ingredients**
**Proteins & Visible Veg**
* **Beef:** 1,500g Chuck Roll (3.5cm chunks, salted)
* **Bacon**: 240g Sliced smoked bacon (chopped)
* **Visible Veg**: 550g Carrot (Batonnets), 480g Button Mushrooms (quartered)
* **Shadow Base:** 340g Onion, 220g Celery both diced, 60g Garlic minced
* **Dark Core:** 58g Tomato Paste
* **Liquid:** 550ml Red Wine (Cab Sauv), 2,400ml Water (Split: braise 1,000ml/ finish 1,400ml) +  2 Beef Stock Cubes
* **Umami & Seasoning:** 1.5 tsp MSG (Split: 0.5 tsp paste/1 tsp braise), 1/4 tsp Allspice (0.5g), 2.5 tsp Dried Thyme (3.5g), 5 Bay Leaves (0.75g), Black Pepper, Salt 2 tsp
* **Beurre Manié:** 125g Flour +50g Butter mixed
**II. Method (Stovetop + Mein Hans)**
1. **Render bacon** in a skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove.
2. Increase skillet heat to high. **Sear chuck roll** in the rendered bacon fat until deeply browned on all sides. Remove.

2. **Sauté Aromatics**: Lower skillet heat to medium. Sauté diced onion, and celery, until deep gold (10 mins). Stir in garlic, tomato paste and MSG. Roast for 4–5 minutes until darkened and fragrant.
3. **Deglaze:** Pour in Red Wine. Boil hard for 6–8 minutes to reduce by 1/3 and scrape up fond. Add water, stock cubes, thyme, bay leaves, allspice, and MSG
4. **Braise**: Run High Pressure for 22 minutes. Perform a **Quick Release**.
5.**Pressure Carrot Cycle:** Add carrot batonnets and sauteed mushroom. Run High Pressure for 4 minutes. Then Quick Release. **Remove and combine** into a big pot.
6. **Thickening**: Pour in the remaining water
7. **Ladle out hot liquid**, whisk smooth with Beurre Manié, and swirl back into the pot. Simmer for 3 minutes until thickened into a dark mahogany glaze.
**Portion-R** 348g: beef 73, veg 75, sauce 200g
**Portion-L** 523g: beef 110, veg 113, sauce 300g

dishes.title: Dark Beer Beef Stew (Target: 7R + 4L)
lines: I. Ingredients
* **Beef**: 1,600g Chuck Roll (3.5cm chunks, salted)
* **Visible Veg**: 625g Potato (3cm cubes), 450g Carrot (2cm oblique), 220g Frozen Peas
* **Shadow Base**: 470g Onion, 250g Celery (both minced), 60g Garlic (minced), Potato off-cuts (minced fine)
* **Dark Core**: 75g Tomato Paste, 45ml Balsamic Vinegar, 1 tsp Brown Sugar (4g)
* **Liquid Input**: 1 Chiangmai Winter can split: 400ml Braise/90ml Cold Finish, 4 Beef Stock Cubes, 1,800ml Water (split: 1000ml / 800ml finish)
* **Umami & Seasoning:** 3 tsp MSG (13.5g, Split: 1 tsp paste / 2 tsp braise), 2 tsp Dried Thyme (2.8g), 5 Bay Leaves (1g), 2.5 tsp Black Pepper (5.75g), salt ½ tsp
* **Beurre Manié**: 90g Flour + 60g Butter mixed into a paste
**II. Method (Hybrid Siemens Induction + Mein Hans)**
1. **Sear chuck roll** in a skillet over high heat until deeply browned on all sides (Use a small amount of oil as needed). Remove.

2. **Sauté Aromatics:** Lower skillet heat to medium. Sauté minced onion, celery, potato off-cuts, and **black pepper** until deep gold. Stir in garlic, tomato paste, and the first portion of the MSG. Roast for 4–5 minutes until darkened and fragrant.
3. **Deglaze:** Pour in Stout. Simmer for 6–8 minutes to reduce and scrape up fond. Add water, stock cubes, thyme, bay leaves, balsamic vinegar, brown sugar, and the second portion of the MSG.
4. **Braise:** Run High Pressure for **22 minutes**. Perform a **Quick Release.**
5. **Pressure Veg Cycle**: Add carrot and potato cubes. Run High Pressure for **4 minutes**. Perform a Quick Release.
6. **Finishing**: Stir in frozen peas and the remaining cold Stout.
7. **Thickening**: Ladle out hot liquid, whisk smooth with Beurre Manié, and swirl back into the pot. Simmer for 3 minutes until thickened into a dark mahogany glaze.
**Portion-R** 348g: beef 73, veg 75, sauce 200g
**Portion-L** 523g: beef 110, veg 113, sauce 300g

dishes.title: Polished Pork Bolognese
lines: **I. Ingredients (20 Portions)**
* **Pork:** 1,000g Minced Pork
* **Base:** Onion 450g, Celery 225g, Carrot 225g finely minced, 60g Garlic minced.
* **The Umami:** Tomato Paste 160g (10 tbsp), Balsamic Vinegar 30ml (2 tbsp), Anchovy Fillet 40g (8 fillets, crushed), 4 Knorr Pork Stock Cubes
* **Fat:** Butter 30g (approx. 2 tablespoons)
* **Liquid:** Polpa 1,600g, Milk 600ml (Split: 400ml for deglazing / 200ml for the final emulsification), 800ml Water (split: 300ml braise / 500ml finish)
* **Seasoning & Spices:** MSG 9g (2 tsp), Nutmeg 0.4g (1/5 tsp), Dried Thyme 2.8g (2 tsp), Black Pepper Heavy crack to finish
**II. Method**

1. **Sear Pork:** Heat pot over high heat with olive oil until smoking. Press the minced pork flat into a single layer. Sear untouched for 4–5 minutes until a deep mahogany crust forms. Flip, break it up briefly, and **remove**. Drain off most rendered fat, leaving ~1 tablespoon in the pan.
2. **Soffritto:** Lower the heat to medium-low. Add the butter, onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté for 15–20 minutes, scraping up browned pork bits, until the veggies turn deep golden.

3. **Aromatics & Paste**: Add the garlic and crushed anchovies; cook for 60 seconds until fragrant. Stir in the tomato paste and balsamic vinegar. Sauté for 2–3 minutes until the paste darkens to a brick-red.
4. **Deglaze:** Pour in milk, pork stock, water. Aggressively scrape every bit of fond off the bottom of the pan and bring to a simmer.
5. **Master Mix**: Return the seared pork. Add the polpa, MSG, nutmeg, and thyme. Stir thoroughly to combine everything into a single uniform mixture.
6. **Braise:** Cook on High Pressure for 30 minutes.QR.

7. **Combine:** Pour in the remaining cold milk and water. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until the milk emulsifies with the pork fat into a thick ragù. Finish with a heavy crack of black pepper and do a final taste test.
**Portion**: 200g

dishes.title: Noir Ragù (Pressure Cooker Edition)
lines: **I. Ingredients** (19 Portions)
* **Meat:** 1,600g Brisket
* **Soffritto:** 400g Onion, 330g Celery (finely minced), 450g Carrot (grated), 80g Garlic minced
* **Umami Boosters:** 12 Anchovy fillets (54g), 3.5 tbsp Worcestershire sauce (50ml), 9.5 tbsp Balsamic Vinegar (140ml), 4 tbsp Brown Sugar (48g)
* **Base:** 4 tbsp Tomato Paste (64g), 680g Canned Polpa, 4 Beef Stock Cubes
* **Liquid:** 500ml Milk (Split: 250ml for stovetop base, 250ml for final finish), 900ml Water (split 500ml braise/400ml final)
* **Spices:** 1 tsp Nutmeg (2.2g), 2 tsp Dried Thyme (2.8g), 2.5 tsp MSG (11g)
* **Mantecatura & Seasoning:** 90g Pecorino (finely grated), black pepper
**II. Method**
1. **Sear the Beef:** Heat a wide skillet on high heat with a splash of oil until smoking. Sear the chuck roll cubes in batches until heavily browned/nearly black on all sides. Remove.
2. **Soffritto:** Lower heat to medium. Add the onions, celery, and grated carrots to the beef fat. Sauté for 15–20 minutes until dark and translucent. Add garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
3. **Melt Anchovies:** Push veggies to the sides of the pan, drop the anchovies into the centre, and stir for 3 minutes until dissolved.
4. **Umami Layer:** Stir in the tomato paste, balsamic vinegar, brown sugar, and Worcestershire sauce. Cook for 5–6 minutes until dark maroon and smelling of toasted caramel.
5. **Deglaze:** Pour in the first split portion of milk, water, and beef stock cubes. Scrape the fond, then bring to a brief simmer.
6. **Master Mix:** Add the polpa, MSG, nutmeg, and thyme. Stir everything thoroughly into a uniform mixture.
7. **Braise:** Transfer the mixture into your pressure cooker pot. Cook on High Pressure for 68 minutes. **QR**. Transfer back to pot.
8. **Shred:** Shred the tender beef into fine strands.
9. Pour in the remaining cold milk. Simmer for 5–8 minutes, stirring continuously, until the sauce thickens and glazes the shredded meat.

10. **Mantecatura:** Turn off the heat completely. Let the pot sit for 60 seconds to drop below boiling. Fold in the 90g finely grated Pecorino and heavy black pepper, stirring vigorously until glossy and completely emulsified.
**Serving:** 200g

dishes.title: Tuscan Pork Braise (Pressure Cooker - 10 Portions)
lines: **I. Ingredients**
* **The Meat**: 1,150g Pork Shoulder, trimmed of hard outer fat, cut into 3-inch.
* **Texture**: 330g Carrot Batonnets, 440g Mushrooms (quartered).
* **Foundation** (Fine Dice): 270g Onion, 110g Carrot, 45g Garlic (smashed).
* **Base:** 900g Mutti Polpa, 2 Knorr Pork Cubes, 1,550ml Water (split 1000ml braise/ 550ml finish)
* **Elements**: 48g Tomato Paste, 4 Anchovy fillets (18g), 1.5 tbsp Oil (21g).
* **Umami**: 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce (10ml), 2 tsp MSG (9g) (Split: 0.5 tsp for paste / 1.5 tsp for braise).
* **Thickener**: 4 tbsp All-Purpose Flour.
* **The Finish**: 4 tsp Balsamic Vinegar (20ml), 2 tsp Brown Sugar (8g).
* **Herbs**: 2 tsp Dried Thyme (2g), 1/2 tsp Salt, and heavy Black Pepper.
**II. The Method (Hybrid Skillet + Mein Hans)**
1. **Flash Sear**: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Season the pork heavily with salt. Flash-sear only two main sides. Remove the meat while the remaining sides are still raw.
2. **Sauté**: Add the diced onion and carrot to the skillet. Cook for 10 minutes until translucent. Stir in the smashed **garlic and thyme**; cook for 1 minute.

3. **Caramelise**: Push the vegetables to the side. Add the anchovy fillets, mashing them into the hot fat until they dissolve. Add the tomato paste and the first MSG. Roast for 2 minutes until it darkens to a brick-red color.
4. **Braise Setup**: Pour in the Mutti Polpa, water, stock cubes, and Worcestershire sauce. Stir in the remaining MSG. Scrape the bottom of the skillet to lift all caramelized fond.
5. **Single Batch Braise** (Mein Hans): Transfer the entire pork and liquid mixture into the pressure cooker. Run on High Pressure for 25 minutes, followed by a Quick Release.

6.  **Combined Veg Cycle**: Add the carrot batonnets and the quartered fresh mushrooms directly into the pressure cooker together. Run on High Pressure for 4 minutes, then perform a **Quick Release**.
7.  **Thickening**: Transfer the contents to a large pot. Whisk water with the flour until smooth, and pour into the pot. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes to activate the starch.
8. **Gloss Finish**: Turn off the heat. Stir in the balsamic vinegar and brown sugar for 30 seconds until the sugar dissolves and the sauce is glossy.
9. **Taste**: Adjust with salt or pepper if needed.
**Portioning**: 355g: Pork 80g, Veg 75g, Sauce 200g.

dishes.title: Pecorino & Broccoli Cream Soup (Pressure Cooker), Target: 10 Portions
lines: **I. Ingredients**
* Meat: 3 Chicken Thighs (skin-on, bone-in, pat dry)
* Broccoli: 500g total (Florets kept tiny, stems diced 3mm)
* Aromatics (3mm dice): 200g Onion, 200g Carrot, 200g Celery, 30g Garlic minced
* Soup Base: 2 whole cans Campbell’s Cream of Mushroom (~800g)
* Water: 1,800ml (for the pressure cycle)
* Milk: 1,700ml (for the stovetop finish)
* Slurry: 105g Flour + room temp water
* Mantecatura: 60g finely grated Pecorino Cheese
* Seasoning: 0.4g Nutmeg (1/3 tsp), 1 tsp MSG (4g), 2 tsp Salt, heavy Black Pepper, 30g butter
**II. The Method**
1.  **Hard Sear**: Heat 2 tbsp oil on medium-high. Sear skin-side down until a dark gold crust forms. Flip for 2 minutes, then remove.
2.  **Sauté the Base**: Lower the heat. Add onion, carrot, celery, and diced broccoli stems. Sauté for 15 minutes. Add garlic and MSG; cook for 2 minutes.
3.  **The Mix**: Whisk the Campbell’s soup base into the sautéed vegetables. Add water until smooth.
4.  **Pressure Braise**: Place chicken thighs and the liquid mix into the pot. Run on High Pressure for 15 minutes. Perform a Quick Release and transfer to your pot.
5.  **Stovetop Finish**: Combine all contents into your pot. Stir in the **milk and the broccoli florets**. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15 minutes until the florets are tender.
6.  **The Shred**: Lift the thighs out, remove bones, shred the meat, and return it to the pot.
7.  **Thickening**: Ladle out hot soup into a bowl, whisk in the Beurre Manié until smooth, and pour the slurry back into the pot. Simmer and stir for 3 minutes.
8.  **Mantecatura**: Turn off the heat. Whisk in the Pecorino, nutmeg, and black pepper until completely glossy and emulsified.
**Portion Size**: 440g

dishes.title: Creamy Chicken Comfort Soup (Pressure Cooker Edition)
lines: **I. Ingredients** (7 Portions)
* **Proteins:** 7 Chicken Thighs (skin-on, bone-in)
* **Fat:** 1 tbsp Olive Oil
* **Aromatics** (Diced): 130g Onion, 180g Carrots, 95g Celery, 16g Garlic minced
* **Base**: 1 can Campbell’s Chicken and Mushroom (400g), 1,000ml Water (braise), 900ml Milk (Stovetop Finish)
* **Thickener**: Slurry: 80g All-purpose Flour
* **Herbs**: 1/8 tsp Nutmeg (0.25g), 1.5 tsp Dried Thyme (1.5g), 1/2 tsp MSG (2.5g)
* **Seasoning**: 20g butter, black pepper and 1.5 tsp Salt
**II. The Method**

1. **The Hard Sear:** Pat dry the chicken thighs. Heat a wide skillet on medium-high with the olive oil. Season the thighs heavily only with salt. Place the thighs skin-side down in the skillet. Sear in batches until a deep, dark gold crust forms. Flip and sear the flesh side for 2 minutes, then remove and set aside on a plate.
2. **Sauté the Base:** Lower heat to medium. Add the diced onion, carrots, and celery directly into the rendered chicken fat. Sauté for 20 minutes until translucent and sweet.
3. Stir in the minced garlic, dried thyme, and MSG. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
4. **The Master Mix:** Whisk together the Campbell’s soup base, the sautéed vegetables, and water until completely smooth.
5. **Pressure Braise:** Place chicken thighs and the Master Mix into the inner pot. Run on High Pressure for 15 minutes. Perform a Quick Release. Remove
6. **The Finish:** Set your pot over medium heat. Stir in milk. Bring to a gentle simmer (uncovered) for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Stir in the nutmeg.

7. **Beurre Manié:** Make slurry with room temp water until completely smooth. Pour the slurry into the pot while stirring gently. Simmer uncovered for 3 minutes to activate the starches and cook out any raw flour taste.
8. Whisk in a heavy crack of black pepper and butter. Do a final taste check and adjust.
**Portion**: ~550g : 1 thigh + soup 330g

dishes.title: Spicy Rosso
lines: **I. Ingredients** (10 Portions)
* Bacon Steak 8pcs, Oil 50g
* Tomato Paste 75g, Knorr cube 1, MSG 1tsp (5g), Thai chilli flakes 1tsp (3.8g), Black Pepper 2.5g
* Rosso 1300g, water 500g
**II. The Method**

1. **Render:** Add 50g oil and bacon lardons into medium-high heat. Let the water purge and completely evaporate (7 mins). When liquid disappears and you hear the sizzle turn from a wet bubble to a fry, drop heat to **medium** to render the fat and crisp the edges without burning**.**
2. **Caramelize & Bloom:** Add tomato paste, crumbled Knorr cube, and directly into the hot fat pool. Stir constantly until the tomato paste turns dark brick-red and smells rich.

3. **Simmer & Reduce:** Pour in hand-crushed tomatoes, MSG, and black pepper. Bring to a boil, then drop heat to medium-low. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until reduced, thick, and glossy orange oil coats the pot edges.
**Portion Size**: 200g: 60g bacon + 140g sauce

dishes.title: Spicy Sausage Cream Ragù
lines: **I. Ingredients** (10 Portions)
* Spicy Italian Sausage 1,000g (casing removed, crumbled)
* Onion 500g (finely diced), Garlic 30g (minced), Mushrooms 400g (diced)
* Tomato Paste 48g, Thyme 1.5g, MSG 5g, Pork Stock Cube 1 cube
* Whole Milk 800ml, Water 500ml
* Salt 10g, Pepper 2.3g
* Beurre Manié: 40g butter + 40g flour
**II. The Method**
1. **Brown the Sausage**: In a large batch pot over medium-high heat, render and brown the 1,000 g crumbled spicy Italian sausage until deeply caramelised.

2. **Sauté Mushrooms & Soffritto**: Add the sliced mushrooms directly into the pot with the sausage (since fat is minimal) and cook until moisture evaporates. Add the 500 g diced onions and 30 g minced garlic; cook until soft.
3. **Pastes & Herbs**: Clear a small space in the centre of the pot. Add tomato paste, and thyme. Stir constantly until dark and fragrant.
4. **Liquids & Seasonings**: Pour in milk, water, crushed stock cube, MSG, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer.

5. **Bind with Beurre Manié**: Add beurre manié to the simmering sauce while whisking. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until the flour cooks out. The consistency should be noticeably lighter and silkier than the previous batch.
**Portion Size**: 200g
